subject: Medsys AI — initial workspace + API key access plan
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@medsys.ai>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv@medsys.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Medsys AI — initial workspace + API key access plan

Hi Elena / Rajiv —

Great to kick off. Per our call today I’m sharing the initial access and activation plan so your infra and security teams can review. Attached is a short checklist and the KMS questionnaire you mentioned. High-level items we’ll complete over the next week: 

- Create Medsys workspace (project namespace) in your chosen region (us-west-2).
- Seed service API keys for integration (scoped: read/generate, short-lived).
- Provision two admin users (Org Admin, Billing Admin) and three developer roles (Dev, SRE, Integration).
- KMS/HSM integration option: customer-managed keys available — see attached worksheet.
- Invite cadence: we’ll send invites in two waves (admins first, then developers).

Quick asks for you to confirm before we proceed:
1) Confirm preferred region (default: us-west-2).
2) Who should be the Org Admin & Billing Admin (name + email).
3) Do you want Redwood to seed initial API keys, or will you generate inside your KMS and share public key material?

I’ll coordinate with Monica (CS ops) and Ben (Solutions) on the handoff once you confirm. If you’d like a short runthrough of the invite flow we can book a 30-min huddle tomorrow.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124

Attachments: medsys-initial-onboard-checklist.pdf (PDF), medsys-kms-requirements.xlsx (XLSX)
From: Elena Park <elena.park@medsys.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@medsys.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Medsys AI — initial workspace + API key access plan

Thanks Vanessa — this looks good and matches what we discussed. A few clarifications: 

- Region: prefer us-east-1 due to our primary infra there. Would that be fine?
- Org Admin: Elena Park (elena.park@medsys.ai)
- Billing Admin: Rajiv Menon (rajiv@medsys.ai)
- Keying: We’d prefer to manage keys in our KMS and provide the public key/thumbprint for Redwood to verify, rather than sharing plaintext API keys. Is that supported?

Technical questions from SRE (copied below):
1) Can Redwood seed ephemeral service tokens scoped to a single project and rotate them daily?
2) We require audit logs for token issuance forwarded to our logging pipeline (Splunk) — do you support an event forwarder or webhook for audit events?

If you can confirm KMS flow and logging options I’ll get the sign-offs from security. A 30-min walk-through tomorrow morning (Aug 19, 9:00am PT) works for us.

Best,
Elena
Product & Security Lead | Medsys AI
elena.park@medsys.ai

Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Medsys AI — initial workspace + API key access plan — internal handoff

Monica / Ben — looping you in to start the implementation runbook. Elena confirmed region = us-east-1 and wants to manage keys in their KMS. Summary & asks below: 

What we know:
- Account: Medsys AI, Deal DEAL-3421.
- Region: us-east-1.
- Admins: Elena (Org Admin), Rajiv (Billing Admin).
- Customer wants to provide public key material from their KMS; Redwood should support verification and issue scoped, ephemeral tokens (preferably rotated daily).

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Ben: Validate KMS public-key verification flow and confirm whether we can issue daily-rotated, project-scoped ephemeral tokens that reference the customer public key. Share proposed token TTL and scope by EOD. (owner: ben.carter)
- Monica: Prepare invite wave 1 (admins) and wave 2 (devs) template emails + enforce MFA requirement in the invite. Also create the initial workspace in us-east-1 and hold until Ben confirms key flow. (owner: monica.patel)
- Vanessa (me): Book the 30-min technical walkthrough for Aug 19 @ 9:00am PT; provide Medsys the KMS worksheet to complete.

Notes on audit logs: customer asked about forwarding token issuance events to Splunk. If we can’t stream directly, consider delivering a daily signed bundle (S3 + signed manifest) as a temporary workaround and follow up with infra to triage long-term pipeline integration.

Please reply with commits / clarifying questions. I’ve attached the customer checklist again for reference.

Thanks,
Vanessa
